questions.q: Where are new conscious memories stored?
a: The hippocampus
The neocortex
The cerebellum
The amygdala
questions.why: Lesson 1 says deliberate new memories, like a neighbor's name, form in the hippocampus.

questions.q: Why are some old memories so vivid?
a: Their parts are stored in many regions
They are repeated every day
They were learned under stress
They sit in a single synapse
questions.why: Lesson 1 says memories spread across sensory areas create more synapses and stronger recall.

a: Spreading study sessions over time helps memory
Repeating a name quickly helps you remember it
Studying in one long block is best
Sleeping after studying erases details
questions.why: Lesson 2 says returning to material after a gap thickens synapses and aids long-term recall.

questions.q: How should you prepare for an exam?
a: Study in shorter sessions, not one long cram
Cram for eight hours the night before
Read the material once without breaks
Focus only on the hardest chapter
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends four two-hour sessions over one eight-hour cram.

questions.q: What does the Zeigarnik effect do?
a: Keeps an unfinished task in mind and sparks ideas
Erases memories that are not repeated
Makes completed tasks easier to forget
Prevents you from starting new projects
questions.why: Lesson 3 says an open loop nags at you and lets your subconscious keep working on the task.
